question: In a pain trial, 40% on the drug and 30% on placebo got relief. What percentage of the drug's responders owe it to the drug?
move: Subtract what the dummy achieved before praising what the real thing did.
trap: Answering 100%, crediting the drug with every patient who got better.
hint: Ask how many of the drug group would have responded to a dummy pill.
steps: Of 100 patients on the drug, 40 get the relief.
About 30 of them would have got it from placebo, as the other arm did.
reference: Laupacis, Sackett & Roberts, An assessment of clinically useful measures of the consequences of treatment, New England Journal of Medicine, 1988
